items.followUp: What appears on the webpage and in the browser tab for this code: <html><body><title>My Page</title></body></html>?

rubric.why: The title element does not display its contents in the webpage area.
rubric.description: States that the webpage area is blank.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for indicating that no text is visibly displayed on the page.

rubric.why: The text inside the title element is used as the document or browser-tab title.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving BISERAWALPINDI as the title.

modelAnswer: No text is displayed in the webpage area; it is blank.
BISERAWALPINDI appears as the document title in the browser tab.

items.followUp: Explain how an IP address helps a computer communicate over a network.

rubric.why: An IP address is a numerical identifier assigned to a device or network interface.
rubric.description: Defines an IP address as a numerical identifier.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a numerical address for a device/interface.

rubric.why: The address identifies a device on a network.
rubric.description: Explains that the address identifies the device on a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its identification purpose.

rubric.why: Network devices use IP addresses to route data to the correct destination.
rubric.description: Explains its role in directing data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning routing or directing data to the destination.

rubric.why: An IPv4 address is 32 bits, commonly written as four decimal numbers separated by dots.
rubric.description: Gives a correct IPv4 format detail.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the 32-bit/four-octet IPv4 format.

modelAnswer: An IP address is a numerical address assigned to a device or network interface.
It identifies the device on a network.
Network devices use IP addresses to route data to the correct destination.
An IPv4 address is 32 bits long and is commonly written as four decimal numbers separated by dots, for example, 192.168.1.1.

items.followUp: What is validation of an algorithm?

rubric.why: Verification checks whether an algorithm or solution is correct.
rubric.description: States that verification is a checking process.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning checking or testing.

rubric.why: The check determines whether the algorithm gives correct results or meets its requirements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning expected results, valid inputs, or requirements.

modelAnswer: Verification is the process of checking or testing an algorithm to ensure that it is correct.
It checks that the algorithm produces the expected results and meets its requirements.

items.followUp: What two resources are commonly used to measure the efficiency of an algorithm?

rubric.why: An algorithm's efficiency includes the time it takes to execute.
rubric.description: Identifies time as an efficiency measure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning execution time or time taken.

rubric.why: An algorithm's efficiency also includes the memory it uses.
rubric.description: Identifies memory use as an efficiency measure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning memory or space used.

modelAnswer: The efficiency of an algorithm is a measure of the resources it needs to solve a problem.
It is commonly measured by its execution time and the memory space it uses.
